lines.text: Do you know how a Wi-Fi password keeps strangers out? The password itself is never sent through the air.
Wi-Fi is just radio. Anyone nearby can pick up every packet, so everything has to be scrambled.
Your phone and the router each turn the password and the network name into the same secret key, on their own.
Then they swap random numbers, and mix them with that key. If both get matching results, each knows the other has the password, without ever saying it.
That creates a fresh key just for this connection, and everything after it is encrypted.
That's why short passwords are risky. On older Wi-Fi, someone who records that handshake can try millions of guesses offline. Newer WPA3 blocks that trick.
Orbi Spaces work like a private network. A Space needs a passcode to join, its files never appear in public, and only members can unlock them.
